$schema_note: RetroForge ticket board. Fields: id, title, phase (roadmap phase), crate (primary write scope), write_scope (globs the executor may touch), depends_on (ticket ids), acceptance (ALL must pass before status=done), points (fibonacci), status (todo|in_progress|done|blocked), notes (OPTIONAL array of strings, append-only: HANDOFF:/BLOCKED: entries). ALWAYS-WRITABLE SET (in addition to write_scope, for every ticket): this file's own-ticket status+notes fields; docs/STATUS.md (append one line per merged ticket); Cargo.lock; docs/TECH_STACK.md section-2 rows (new-dependency decision record). Claim rule: a ticket is claimable when all depends_on are done. Executors: work ONE ticket per session, run `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace && scripts/validate-arch.sh` plus ticket acceptance before marking done. Never widen write_scope beyond the always-writable set without a HANDOFF note in the ticket's notes array.

Probed live against SingleStepTests/spc700 (git 2.55.0): fetch-by-bare-SHA is allowed by GitHub, 1.4s/96MB. Timestamps must NOT be used (mtimes are not in git; committer dates are rewritable and non-monotonic across merges). CI TRAP: actions/checkout@v4 defaults to fetch-depth 1, and on a shallow clone these commands silently degrade — validate-evidence.mjs would pass while enforcing nothing, which is this project's known fake-success failure mode. fetch-depth: 0 plus an explicit `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` guard are acceptance requirements, not niceties.

notes: CLOSED 2026-08-03 (conductor). All four acceptance criteria verified INDEPENDENTLY (RF-L-08): full seven-command gate re-run by the conductor, all exit 0, 213 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored with vectors absent. THE SEAM HELD — verified structurally, not on the agent's word: `master_cycle` is mutated only inside crates/rf-nes/src/system/mod.rs (CpuBus::read, CpuBus::write, run_oam_dma), and `grep -rn 'stall|dma' crates/rf-nes/src/cpu/` returns NOTHING, so the CPU has no knowledge of DMA at all. W1-02 was therefore an addition, not the rewrite the risk note feared. OAM DMA cycle counts re-derived by the conductor against nesdev: 1 dummy + (0 or 1) alignment + 256 get/put pairs (512) = 513/514, and the tests assert master_cycle parity as an explicit PRECONDITION before triggering, so neither branch can silently be exercised twice.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor): the DMC/OAM-DMA seam flagged in HANDOFF resolves in favour of the current design, and EMULATION_CORES.md section 1 is the authority: 'CPU is the master clock. Each chip keeps its own cycle counter; when the CPU touches a register another chip owns, that chip runs catch_up(to_master_cycle) first.' So the master cycle counter must live in the SYSTEM BUS and be advanced inside CpuBus::read/write (one tick per bus op), NEVER by summing Cpu::step's u32 return afterwards. Only then do bus-inserted stall cycles (OAM DMA's 513/514, later DMC) land in the master clock for free, and the $2007/$4016 RDY double-read glitch becomes expressible as the bus performing the read twice internally and returning the second value. If the executor finds itself needing to add DMA cycles to step()'s return value, that is the signal the seam did NOT hold — stop and escalate rather than papering over it.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor): rf-nes has NO dependency on rf-cart today and must add one (path dep; permitted — validate-arch.sh rule 1 forbids only upper-layer crates and rf-cart is a peer core crate, rule 3 exempts rf-nes). Note rf-cart exposes cartridge METADATA only: `Cartridge::load(&[u8]) -> Result<Cartridge, CartError>` yielding `Cartridge::Nes { header: NesHeader, identity: RomIdentity }`, where NesHeader carries format/mapper/submapper/prg_rom_size/chr_rom_size/prg_ram_size/mirroring/battery/trainer — but NOT the PRG/CHR bytes. rf-nes must slice those out of the raw image itself (16-byte header + optional 512-byte trainer offset). rf-cart is outside this ticket's write scope, so do not 'fix' it there.

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor): crates/rf-nes/Cargo.toml's description and src/lib.rs's module doc both claim rf-nes 'consumes rf-core-api only'. That is already inaccurate (there is no rf-core-api dependency either) and adding rf-cart makes it more so — update both in this ticket (they are in scope) rather than leaving an R-15 stale-comment.

acceptance: trace logger in nestest.log format (FR-DBG-003)

notes: CLOSED 2026-08-03 (conductor). Both acceptance criteria verified INDEPENDENTLY (RF-L-08): full seven-command gate re-run, all exit 0, 238 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. Result is FULL-LINE byte-exact 8991/8991 — the disassembly column (FR-DBG-003) as well as PC/A/X/Y/P/SP/CYC (FR-CORE-021), not the register-columns-only fallback the brief permitted. ANTI-TAMPER PROOF (the check that matters, since a comparison that passes vacuously looks identical to one that works): the conductor corrupted the A: register on line 5001 of a copy of the golden log and re-ran — the suite reported exactly '8990 matched, 1 mismatched, first divergence at line 5001' and FAILED. The diff is real and byte-exact, not a loosened comparison. Evidence now covers 2 Tier-A-local suites (nes6502 2,560,000 cases + nestest 8991 lines).

SCRUTINIZED 2026-08-03 (conductor): the agent's one semantic judgment call — hardcoding $FF in NesBus::peek for the APU stub range so the disassembly annotation matches — was checked against the real log rather than accepted. It holds: all five golden lines ($4004-$4007, $4015) show '= FF' while the accumulator on those same lines holds 02/3F/9A/FF/00, so an open-bus latch cannot explain a constant FF. The fix is also correctly scoped — `peek` is side-effect-free and used ONLY for the trace annotation; `read_untimed`, the real emulation path, keeps its true open-bus latch and is unchanged. Not a fudge to force a match.

FLAKE FIXED 2026-08-03 (conductor): the agent honestly reported two one-off non-reproducible test flakes. They were a real race, not noise: three copies of a `tempdir()` helper (fetch.rs, nes6502_evidence.rs, nestest_evidence.rs) keyed the directory on `process::id() + SystemTime nanos`, but libtest runs a binary's tests in PARALLEL THREADS sharing one pid, so two threads in the same clock tick get the same path and one test's cleanup deletes the other's working directory. Added an AtomicU64 sequence to all three; 3 consecutive rf-harness runs green (82 passed each). Left in place because an intermittently-red gate corrodes the entire independent-verification discipline this project runs on.

SCOPE-ADD 2026-08-03 (conductor): nestest's ROM and golden log are fetched, gitignored artifacts (NFR-006), so like the nes6502 vectors this suite CANNOT run in CI and `cargo test --workspace` must pass when they are absent. That makes it the second Tier-A-local suite and exactly what W0-07's evidence gate exists for — without an evidence row, a passing nestest is invisible to CI and unverifiable. Added the four exact paths needed to register it (scripts/local-gate.sh, scripts/validate-evidence.mjs, docs/evidence/local-gate.json, docs/TESTING.md) rather than widening to scripts/** or docs/**. CI still never fetches anything (HP-4: Brad is GitHub-Actions-constrained).

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor, verified against the real fetched log): nestest.log is 8991 lines and CRLF-terminated — strip the trailing \r or every single line diff fails. The register block begins at byte offset 48; the disassembly field is columns 0..47, space-padded. First line is `C000  4C F5 C5  JMP $C5F5` with A:00 X:00 Y:00 P:24 SP:FD PPU:  0, 21 CYC:7 — i.e. the trace starts AFTER a 7-cycle reset, which is why this ticket must build the reset sequence W1-02 deferred. PPU column format is `PPU:%3d,%3d` (space-padded, e.g. 'PPU:  0, 21' and 'PPU:233,209').

PRE-FLIGHT 2026-08-03 (conductor): THE PPU COLUMN NEEDS NO PPU. Verified arithmetically over all 8991 lines with ZERO mismatches: scanline == (CYC*3)//341 and dot == (CYC*3)%341, exactly. So the trace logger can emit a byte-exact PPU column from the CPU cycle count alone. Do NOT build or stub a PPU to satisfy it — the PPU is W1-04a, and this holds only because nestest's automated mode leaves rendering disabled (no odd-frame skipped dot).

HANDOFF 2026-08-03 (conductor, from W1-02): W1-02 deliberately did NOT build a reset sequence — `NesBus::new` starts `master_cycle` at 0 and W1-02's tests set `cpu.pc` directly. Two consequences this ticket must absorb, both already documented in crates/rf-nes/src/system/mod.rs's `run_oam_dma` doc: (1) nestest's $C000 entry needs a real reset/power-on sequence (reset vector fetch, correct initial SP/P, and the 7-cycle reset timing) or the CYC column will be offset from the golden log from the first line; (2) until that sequence anchors the master-clock PHASE to hardware, OAM DMA's get/put parity is an internal bookkeeping convention rather than a hardware-true absolute — so a real ROM's DMA cost can differ from the model by exactly one cycle. Scoping the reset sequence into this ticket is the intended fix. Both are honest documented deferrals, not defects.
